newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Reliance unveils generous bonus issue.
newsitem.headline: India's Reliance unveils generous bonus issue.

text.p: India's largest private company Reliance Industries on Thursday ended weeks of feverish stockmarket guessing by giving its shareholders a huge reward with a one-for-one bonus share issue.
The petrochemicals and textile giant also said it did not foresee any further equity dilution during the next two or three years.
"The bonus offer reflects our confidence in the future," Chairman Dhirubhal Ambani told a packed annual shareholders meeting.
"We do not foresee any further equity dilution over the next two to three years, excluding outstanding conversions (of debentures)," Ambani added.
The bonus issue was more generous than the market had expected, traders said.
Some had expected the company to announce an issue of three shares for every five shares held -- the same ratio as Reliance's last two bonus issues in the 1980s.
At 0950 GMT, Reliance shares were quoted at 377.50 rupees, up 11 rupees or just over three percent, on the Bombay stock exchange.
Reliance began as a commodities trading firm in 1958 and built itself into India's biggest private-sector company.
Ambani said sales were expected to reach 200 billion rupees ($5.5 billion) by the year 2000. Sales in 1996/97 to March 31 totalled 87.3 billion rupees, up from 77.86 billion the previous year.
"Based on firm plans, our sales are expected to approach the 200 billion rupees milestone by the year 2000," he said.
"We have set ourselves targets of achieving 20 percent compound growth in earnings per share and a return of 20 percent on shareholders funds over the next five years," Ambani added.
Ambani also said Reliance planned to follow international accounting practices in addition to the domestic accounting standards.
"We will...be reconciling our accounts in line with U.S. GAAP (general accepted accounting principles) standards from the current year," he said, noting that the company had a global investor base.
Since 1992, Reliance has raised $1.5 billion from international markets that included global depositary receipts (GDRs), Eurobonds, and a 100-year bond in the United States. ($1 = 35.82 rupees)
